questions.q: What does a DBA own on a traditional on-prem SQL Server, per this lesson?
options: Everything above the concrete floor — hardware, OS patching, SQL Server patching, storage, networking, backups, and HA/DR
Only the SQL Server installation itself, nothing else
Only the database schema and queries, never the infrastructure
Nothing — infrastructure teams handle all of it separately from the DBA
questions.explain: On-prem means total ownership of every layer, from hardware through HA/DR, which is also total responsibility.

questions.q: Why is "Azure SQL" described as an umbrella term rather than a single product?
options: Because it covers a family of different ways to run SQL Server-compatible workloads in Azure, each moving a different slice of ownership to Microsoft
Because Microsoft renamed SQL Server to Azure SQL with no other changes
Because it refers only to Azure SQL Database and nothing else
Because it is just marketing language with no technical meaning
questions.explain: The three concrete options — Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, and SQL Server on an Azure VM — each sit under this umbrella with a different ownership split, covered in full in Lesson 3.

questions.q: What is the real shift Azure SQL makes, according to this lesson?
options: Which responsibilities move to Microsoft and which stay with you — not simply relocating the same server to the cloud
There is no real shift; Azure SQL behaves identically to on-prem SQL Server in every respect
Azure SQL removes the need for a DBA entirely
Azure SQL only changes where the physical hardware sits, nothing about responsibilities
questions.explain: The tempting but misleading framing is "the same server, somewhere else." The accurate framing is a changed ownership split that differs by deployment option.

questions.q: What replaces OS-patching concerns for a DBA once that responsibility moves to Microsoft?
options: Capacity planning, cost management, and understanding exactly which configuration knobs are still available
Nothing — the DBA role has no remaining responsibilities
Writing more T-SQL queries against the database
Manually SSHing into the underlying VM to verify patches anyway
questions.explain: The job changes shape rather than disappearing — a task that stops being yours is replaced by different, still-real DBA work.

questions.q: Why does this lesson come before Lesson 3's side-by-side comparison of the three deployment options?
options: Because understanding that there's an ownership trade, and what's being traded, is the prerequisite for choosing correctly between the specific options
Because Lesson 3 requires no conceptual foundation and the ordering is arbitrary
Because this lesson teaches T-SQL syntax that Lesson 3 depends on
Because Lesson 3 only covers on-prem SQL Server, not Azure options
questions.explain: This lesson sets up the ownership-split framing that Lesson 3 applies concretely to Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, and SQL Server on an Azure VM.
